title: Keep gateway routing policy aligned with user profiles
problem: The gateway profile uses a reduced legacy provider and group topology, so its fallback and provider-selection behavior can diverge from the canonical user profile.
outcome: Gateway and user profiles use the same provider-group, health-check, fallback, and final-route policy while retaining their distinct provider sources and gateway runtime envelope.

actors.name: Profile user
actors.responsibility: Receive a predictable automatic proxy route with the same LIVE and SEED recovery behavior across profile types.

actors.name: Service operator
actors.responsibility: Render the gateway from its direct upstream sources without changing server runtime settings or publishing user feeds.

in_scope: Align provider names, health-check settings, proxy groups, fallback order, group membership, and MATCH behavior with the current user renderer.
Keep the gateway provider URL on the configured direct upstream and the user provider URL on the published subctl feed.
Keep gateway BASE defaulted to PROXY and user BASE defaulted to DIRECT as an explicit profile-specific selection default.
Retain acceptance of the legacy provider_download_proxy setting while retiring its effect on the gateway fetch route.
out_of_scope: Changing production configuration, rendering production files, restarting services, or deploying a release.
Changing gateway TUN, DNS, listeners, controller, interface, protected hosts, or direct bootstrap rules.
Changing user or gateway provider source URLs or moving the gateway onto a published provider feed.

invariants.claim: Both renderers use the same canonical provider-backed group topology, provider health checks, LIVE-to-SEED fallback, and provider-fetch recovery order.
invariants.enforcement: A structural projection of generated user and gateway profiles compares providers and policy groups, allowing only declared source and BASE-default differences.

invariants.claim: The user profile uses the published provider source and the gateway uses the direct configured upstream source; neither source is substituted for the other.
invariants.enforcement: Renderer tests assert source URLs by profile type and ensure gateway output contains no public feed base URL or shared token.

invariants.claim: The gateway keeps BASE selected as PROXY by default, user profiles keep DIRECT, and MATCH targets BASE in both profiles.
invariants.enforcement: Profile tests assert both selected defaults and the shared final MATCH route.

invariants.claim: Gateway-specific TUN, DNS, listeners, controller, interface, and direct bootstrap routing remain intact.
invariants.enforcement: Gateway profile tests assert these exact sections and the direct bootstrap-rule prefix alongside the shared policy projection.

invariants.claim: Existing configuration containing provider_download_proxy continues to load, but the field no longer changes canonical gateway provider-fetch routing.
invariants.enforcement: Config compatibility and gateway routing tests cover legacy file and settings-overlay values; the operator UI and documentation identify the setting as deprecated.

invariants.claim: No production render or redeploy occurs as part of this change.
invariants.enforcement: Verification uses synthetic fixtures and local generated profiles only.

failure_model.failure: The validated provider cache cannot produce a usable SEED snapshot when gateway profiles are rendered.
failure_model.response: Fail rendering with the existing seed validation error and leave the current gateway output untouched.

failure_model.failure: The gateway or user source is accidentally changed while policy is shared.
failure_model.response: Fail the structural/source assertions before any production release.

failure_model.failure: A gateway-specific runtime section changes as a side effect of policy extraction.
failure_model.response: Fail the exact gateway-envelope assertions and restore the section from the pre-change behavior.

acceptance_signals: User and gateway generated profiles have matching canonical provider and group policy, with only documented source and BASE-default differences.
The direct gateway provider source, gateway runtime sections, and bootstrap rule prefix remain correct.
The full project test suite passes and generated profiles pass the configured Mihomo validation/runtime checks.
The implementation reports a structural diff and does not alter production state.
